title: Pneumonia
subtitle: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus. It can range from mild to serious and potentially fatal, especially in the elderly, infants, and immunocompromised individuals.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Pneumonia is the leading infectious cause of death worldwide, killing over 2.5 million people annually. Bacterial pneumonia is the most common form in adults.
items: Chest pain that worsens when breathing or coughing
Cough producing phlegm (yellow, green, or bloody)
Fever, sweating, and chills
Shortness of breath even with normal activities
Fatigue and loss of appetite
Confusion or altered mental status in elderly

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Pneumonia can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi. The cause determines the appropriate treatment.
items: Streptococcus pneumoniae, most common bacterial cause in adults
Influenza virus and SARS-CoV-2, common viral causes
Mycoplasma pneumoniae, causes walking pneumonia
Pneumocystis jirovecii, fungal pneumonia in immunocompromised

sections.title: Prevention
items: Pneumococcal vaccine (PCV13, PPSV23) for high risk groups
Annual influenza vaccine reduces pneumonia risk
COVID-19 vaccination
Wash hands frequently and avoid touching face
Do not smoke, smoking damages lung defenses
Adequate nutrition and rest to maintain immune function

sections.title: Treatment
items: Antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia, Amoxicillin, Azithromycin
Antivirals for viral pneumonia (e.g. Oseltamivir for flu-related)
Oxygen therapy for low blood oxygen levels
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Hospitalization for severe cases or high risk patients
ICU care with ventilator support for critical pneumonia

facts: No. 1 infectious cause of child deaths worldwide
1, 3 weeks for mild; 4, 6 weeks for severe
